newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China awaits lower soybean, meal prices - traders.
newsitem.headline: China awaits lower soybean, meal prices - traders.

text.p: Grains traders in China and Hong Kong said on Tuesday their Chinese customers were not tempted by Monday's drop in soybean futures and were waiting for lower prices.
"China is not so interested today because they are expecting even lower prices," said one China-based source.

Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures ended lower on Monday, with July down 16 at $8.38-1/2 on weather forecasts showing ideal growing conditions in the United States and more talk that U.S. firms were importing South American supplies.
Traders said China's soybean and meal buying over the past couple of weeks had covered nearby positions and that any enquiries were for forward shipments.
China was looking for new crop soybeans priced at US$280 per tonne, C&F China, for November delivery. Meal priced at roughly those levels would also be attractive, dealers said.
"We've had a few enquiries but they're not very serious," said one trader.
